title: fix(agents): a subagent's previous result is lost when its next turn starts quickly
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a completed subagent (for example a visible child in a managed worktree) is given its next turn before its previous result has been announced, the previous turn's announcement to the parent is dropped. The log shows `Subagent announce failed: ... transcript identity changed during announcement.`, and the parent only ever hears about the later turn.

## User Impact

Each completed turn keeps its own parent announcement and receipt while the child continues working, so parents no longer miss results from quick follow-ups. Child transcripts were never affected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary follow-up admission in `reactivateCompletedSubagentSession` went through steer replacement, which retired the completed run's registry row along with its pending delivery owner. Follow-ups now preserve the completed execution through the registry row owner (`mutateSubagentRuns`). A superseded run that still owes its completion is announced instead of retired, and the new turn gets independent successor authority. Delivery stays bound to the exact execution, and the predecessor's session effects stay fenced from the newer turn. Paused continuation and steer keep their replacement behavior. No schema change. Production LOC +96/-65.

## Evidence

- Found by a live run on an isolated Gateway with a real model: in the managed-worktree scenario, turn 2 was admitted about 1 s after turn 1 completed, and turn 1's parent announcement was never delivered. The same loss shows up in stopped databases from builds before the registry redesign (#163195), so this is pre-existing.
- The regression drives registered agent admission with paused transcript-read and delivery-admission boundaries, distinct per-turn outputs, durable receipts, restored pending delivery, and replay deduplication. It fails on main and passes for all three interleavings (4.66 s, 2.85 s, 2.39 s).
- On the initial reviewed head `761171d03b00`, 846 focused announce/reactivation/registry cases passed across 18 files. `pnpm tsgo:core`, all 27 affected test type graphs, typed lint, oxfmt, deslop, and `git diff --check` pass. Codex autoreview through P2 is scoped-clean.
- Production final-effect authority proof now passes for allowed delivery and independent predecessor/successor revocation; the exact cases and boundary are below. Live managed-worktree/concurrency confirmation remains a separate landing gate.


### CI follow-up

The initial CI run [36977686534](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36977686534) exposed stale retirement expectations in four sibling suites, a benchmark caller still using the renamed cleanup callback, and a fixture dispatch-pump race in the new Gateway regression. The assertions now require retained predecessor custody and independent successor identity; the Gateway fixture waits for the actual command-entry signal instead of pumping fake timers over real worker persistence. No runtime behavior or timeout budget was changed by these repairs.

The unrelated worker-placement lint failure was repaired on main by `95a67da528c7`; main was merged without conflicts. The reviewed PR patch has the same stable patch ID before and after that merge. Fresh Codex autoreview through P2 is scoped-clean. All 27 affected test type graphs, script types, typed lint, formatting, and diff checks passed for the repaired candidate; the inherited lint check also passed after integration.

The integrated head `fe4a273af918929f93e5ce5d6310d57077813734` passes 445 focused tests across five files with `--maxWorkers=1`. Gateway methods took 82.92 s; announcement-worker and steering tests together took 55.44 s; cancellation publication took 37.68 s; requester-wake commit took 9.92 s (Vitest wall times). Individual pre-integration one-worker file times were 79.44 s, 17.11 s, 62.59 s, and 17.17 s for announcement-worker, steering, publication, and requester-wake respectively. These existing integration fixtures exercise registered admission, worker settlement, or the parent turn and were updated without adding cases. The recovery-sweep benchmark also passed (1.71 s, zero session effects).

The inherited duplicate logger field, Doctor fixture lint errors, and custody import cycle were subsequently repaired on main by `d81a2d8b7294` and `0f470aecdc12`; those fixes are included through a conflict-free main merge.


### Final-effect authority proof

[`server.native-completion-authority.test.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6695946a45fb05b10352d7a1f74d711102ff01e7/src/gateway/server.native-completion-authority.test.ts) now exercises two registered executions in one child session through real Gateway admission. Both completion announcements are held immediately before the real requester input writer, after the successor was admitted. Each execution has a separately revocable operator source. The test controls model output; child transcript writes/reads, announcement dispatch, requester authorization, input/transcript persistence, dedupe, and delivery receipts use the production owners.

| Source revoked while announcements are in flight | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Neither | Both results persist exactly once, with distinct run keys and their own source authority. Both delivery receipts succeed. |
| Predecessor | Its requester input and command are rejected; it receives no successful delivery receipt or dedupe entry. The successor still delivers once under its own authority. |
| Successor | Its requester input and command are rejected; it receives no successful delivery receipt or dedupe entry. The predecessor still delivers once under retained custody. |

All three cases pass. Resuming both completed runs produces no duplicate requester input or command. A temporary borrowed-authority mutation failed all three cases for the intended reasons: wrong source identity with both sources live, zero deliveries instead of one after predecessor revocation, and two instead of one after successor revocation. The production file was restored byte-for-byte; no production defect or additional runtime change was needed.

Validation: 43 focused tests passed across native completion, registered custody, and reactivation suites. The final native file replay passed all 12 cases after the assertion lint correction. Affected `gateway-server` tsgo graph, typed lint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and fresh delta autoreview through P2 pass. With `--maxWorkers=1`, the three new cases initially took 1.90 s / 2.25 s / 1.14 s; the final full-file run took 95.45 s wrapper wall (91.05 s Vitest wall) under concurrent local validation. The suite reuses one Gateway; this contract needs real admission and persistence to observe revoked final effects. No timeout, retry, or worker configuration was relaxed.

Current head: `6695946a45fb05b10352d7a1f74d711102ff01e7`. [Exact-head CI run 36983990346](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36983990346) passed. The three new cases also passed in CI in 2.433 s / 1.120 s / 0.975 s (4.528 s combined case time). [ClawSweeper revision 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163352#issuecomment-5947303422) explicitly resolves the authority-proof blocker and reports no actionable findings or remaining pre-merge items. Native preparation is complete at this head. No merge has been submitted; the external exact-head live-proof gate remains in force.
